stories.topic: US / SINGAPORE / CHINA / AI / SEMICONDUCTORS / TRADE CONTROLS / NVDA
stories.headline: New US chip-export rule requires licences for advanced chips supplied to firms in Singapore and four other countries
stories.body: The US Commerce Department issued restrictions on overseas data-centre access to advanced AI chips, intended to limit circumvention through remote computing. Covered advanced-chip exports to companies in Singapore, Thailand, Malaysia, Indonesia and Brazil require licences, subject to the rule details and exemptions. Reuters reports exclusions for online-retailer and social-media systems and rescission of the earlier broader licensing framework. No directly attributable Nvidia, FX or Treasury-yield movement was verified.
stories.analysis: Licensing could affect procurement timetables, compliance costs and demand for cloud compute; commercial and earnings effects cannot be quantified from the announcement alone.
stories.watch_next: Commerce implementation details, licence determinations, export-compliance responses and any company guidance.

stories.topic: GLOBAL MARKETS / OIL / SHIPPING / HORMUZ / CHINA / INFLATION
stories.headline: Gulf of Oman-to-China oil-supertanker rates 64% below October peak
stories.body: Reuters reports Gulf of Oman-to-China VLCC freight assessments of about 308 Worldscale on 13 November versus 841 on 8 October, approximately 64% lower. Recovering Gulf exports, reduced longer-haul crude demand and additional vessel availability contributed. This is a historical comparison of two dated assessments, not a 64% decline within this reporting window or a live charter quote. Shipping attacks and security risks continued.
stories.analysis: If sustained, lower VLCC rates may reduce seaborne crude transport costs, though actual oil prices, insurance and delivered fuel costs may follow different paths.
stories.watch_next: Baltic Exchange route assessments, independently verified exports, insurance and physical Hormuz shipping.

stories.topic: US / CHINA / RUSSIA / NORTH KOREA / GEOPOLITICS / TRADE
stories.headline: Kremlin details Xi-Putin-Trump summit and Trump floats possible Kim attendance
stories.body: The Kremlin said Putin, Xi and Trump planned a Thursday meeting during the APEC summit in Shenzhen, at the Chinese leader's residence. Trump separately said he might meet North Korea's Kim Jong Un in China. The Kim meeting was not confirmed. These are plans and conditional statements, not completed meetings, agreements or verified market reactions.
stories.analysis: A meeting could change trade and security expectations, but invitations and political statements are not negotiated policy outcomes.
stories.watch_next: Official meeting confirmations and substantive statements on chip controls, Taiwan, sanctions, North Korea and Russia-Ukraine.

stories.topic: US / AI / DATA CENTRES / ENERGY / REGULATORY RISK
stories.headline: New study measures US hyperscale data-centre emissions and electricity concentration
stories.body: A peer-reviewed study reported by Reuters estimates 25.7 million tonnes of CO2 from 403 US hyperscale data centres during May 2024-April 2025, about three times the earlier 2018 reference. Virginia, Oregon, Ohio and Iowa accounted for more than half of the electricity use studied. These historical emissions estimates do not measure current output, future financial costs or an observed equity, utility-price or bond-spread reaction.
stories.analysis: Electricity availability and potential local permitting or environmental constraints could affect AI infrastructure costs; historical emissions are not future expenditure or current stock prices.
stories.watch_next: Site-specific power contracts, local regulation, build-out costs and the study’s measurement caveats.
